messages:
anna-peopleops: Quick question for managers with international reports: how do promotions + comp changes work for EMEA/APAC hires? Any extra steps? :earth_africa:

marco-manager: We have an EMEA engineer (based in Ireland) up for L5 promotion. Main worries: currency conversion, local benefits eligibility, and equity grant timing.

yuki-hr: Good callout. For international employees you must 1) include the local People Ops partner in the packet, 2) attach local market data (country-specific), and 3) confirm local labor rules (e.g., statutory notice).

anna-peopleops: To add: in the promotion packet include a line: "Local HR partner: <name>" and upload local compensation benchmarks (local currency). Comp committee prefers amounts normalized to USD in the attachments but needs raw local currency too.

marco-manager: If we propose a salary that, when converted, exceeds the local band top, does that require the same VP + exception flow?

yuki-hr: Yes  exceptions still need VP approval. Also include two local market comps (from local surveys) and note any tax/take-home impacts for the employee.

olga-payroll: Operational notes from payroll: EMEA payroll cutoff dates can differ by country. For Ireland the payroll feed cutoff to hit the 1st-of-month pay is the 20th prior month (not the 12th). Always check local payroll schedule in the packet checklist.

compbot: [automated] Reminder: For international comp requests, set field "cross-border"=true in the form. Packets missing local HR partner will be returned.

marco-manager: Equity timing: should we delay promotion until after next global grant cycle or grant pro-rated RSUs now?

yuki-hr: Two options: 1) pro-rated grant at promotion (requires comp+rewards approval), or 2) wait for next refresh cycle. If retention risk exists, flag the packet "equity urgent" and include rationale.

olga-payroll: Also note: different countries have different vesting/reporting rules for RSUs. Coordinate with Rewards when asking for pro-rated equity.

anna-peopleops: Question about effective dates: can we backdate promotions to match project milestones?

yuki-hr: We avoid backdating to before the manager's sign-off. Small retro within 30-day payroll retro window is automatic; retro beyond 30 days needs exec sign-off and legal review in some jurisdictions.

marco-manager: What about probation/visa implications for newly converted contractors? The hire team mentioned visa start date constraints.

yuki-hr: If visa/work permit start date differs from the effective comp date, include immigration note in packet. For conversions, Recruiting + Local HR must confirm visa eligibility before comp is finalized.

olga-payroll: Practical: include preferred pay currency and whether employee wants local bank vs global payroll. This affects taxes and timing.

anna-peopleops: Any docs we should attach beyond the usual (just to save back-and-forth)?

yuki-hr: Attach: 1) local market comp snapshot, 2) confirmation from local HR partner, 3) proposed local salary + USD equivalent, 4) any visa/immigration notes, 5) equity ask rationale if applicable.

marco-manager: Timeline question: employee's requested effective date is 2026-09-01 (month start). Ireland cutoff is 2026-08-20 per olga. When do we need to submit?

olga-payroll: For Ireland: packet fully approved + payroll feed in by 2026-08-18 to be safe. If comp approval lands after that, we'll process and retro within 30-day window as long as approvals are complete by 2026-09-30.

compbot: [automated] Note: Intl comp committee review slot on 2026-08-05 (EMEA timezone). Submit packets with international flag by 2026-07-28 for consideration.

anna-peopleops: Thanks all. I'll update the international promo checklist and add the Ireland cutoff table. Marco, ping me and Yuki before you submit and we can do a quick pre-check. :thumbsup:
